hints.title: Premature Discard Greedy Trap Obstacle
hints.text: Greedy choices that discard characters too early can prevent forming the lexicographically smallest result. How can tracking the final occurrence of each character decide whether a larger predecessor can be safely evicted?

hints.title: Monotonic Eviction with Safety Invariant
hints.text: A preceding character can be safely evicted if it is lexicographically larger than the current character and its last occurrence index appears later in the string.

hints.title: Monotonic Character Eviction Procedure
hints.text: Precompute the last occurrence index for every unique character. Iterate through s: if ch is already in the result sequence, skip it. Otherwise, while the result is non-empty, its last character is > ch, and that last character occurs again later, pop it. Append ch and mark it seen.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Each character is pushed and popped at most once; auxiliary storage bounded by 26 characters.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute-force generation of all valid duplicate-free subsequences takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Alphabet size bounded to 26 limits the auxiliary lookup table to O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Managing both the monotonic order condition and the remaining-count safety check simultaneously.
